title: Running the Development Server
description: Fire up the built‑in server and see your app live.

slides.title: Start the Server
slides.content: Navigate into your project folder (where `manage.py` is) and run:

slides.title: What Happens? 🖥️
slides.content:
You’ll see output like:

```
Starting development server at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
Quit the server with CONTROL-C.
```

**Open a browser** and go to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`. You’ll see the Django welcome page – congratulations! Your first project is alive.

quizData.question: What is the default port used by Django’s development server?
quizData.explanation: Django runs on port 8000 by default. You can change it with `python manage.py runserver 8080`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Keep the server running

The development server automatically reloads when you change code – you don’t need to restart it manually (except when adding new files or installing packages).
